all_questions.question: [meteorology: forecast verification + operations research: newsvendor] Is the model's committed infarct volume a Dice-optimal hedge — a bet shaped by the scoring rule — rather than its calibrated belief, shrinking below its own expected volume exactly in the most uncertain patients?

[photography: rolling-shutter / snapshot-timing artifact] Is the model using the CTA's acquisition-timing luck — where in the patient's own bolus transit the snapshot was caught — as if it were collateral biology?

[metrology: inter-laboratory round-robin / gauge R&R] Is the model using icobrain's dialect of the perfusion maps rather than the hemodynamics beneath, so its predictions move when the same raw bolus movie is deconvolved by a different published formula?

[economics: hedonic pricing] Is the benchmark using a flat value function — errors priced identically in the internal capsule and in silent white matter — while the released 3-month mRS prices them apart?

[ecology/climate science: early-warning signals] Does penumbral tissue near collapse show critical slowing down — rising temporal autocorrelation in its 4D enhancement residuals — and does the model read it?

[cardiology/signal processing: heart-rate-variability analysis] Is the model reading atrial fibrillation — the stroke's embolic cause — as beat-to-beat jitter written into the 4D contrast enhancement?

[electrical network theory: effective resistance] Does the Circle-of-Willis graph's effective resistance between inflow and the occluded territory predict what the model spares, making the released CoW masks a collateral-capacity gauge?
[forensic accounting: Benford/digit forensics] Do the perfusion maps' value distributions carry a processing watermark — and is the model reading the watermark rather than the physiology?

candidates.title: The forecaster's hedge: the model's volume is a bet, not a belief
candidates.question: Is the model using a Dice-optimal hedging policy — committing less lesion volume than its own probabilistic evidence expects, and more so the more uncertain the case — so that challenge-model volumes are bets shaped by the scoring rule rather than calibrated beliefs?

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: Hedging under improper scoring rules (meteorological forecast verification: a forecaster scored by the wrong rule reports a strategically shifted forecast, not their true belief) combined with the newsvendor critical fractile (operations research: the quantity a rational agent commits reveals the cost ratio its objective imposes).
cross_domain.implied_measurement: Compare, per case, the model's committed volume against two quantities computed from its own soft output: its expected volume under calibration (the belief) and the zero-parameter expected-Dice-optimal volume (the bet the scoring rule dictates). Hedging = the committed volume tracks the bet, not the belief, with the gap growing in case uncertainty.
cross_domain.if_analogy_dropped: The study degrades to a standard calibration/volume-bias audit — still runnable, but it loses the zero-parameter quantitative prediction (committed volume should equal the expected-Dice-optimal volume) that turns 'miscalibrated' into 'hedging as the objective dictates'.

candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using the scoring rule, not only the scan: its committed infarct volume is the Dice-optimal bet, shrinking below its own expected volume as case uncertainty grows — so segmentation-derived volumes systematically understate the lesion in exactly the uncertain patients where a volume matters most.
candidates.X_measurement: From the model's own soft output p (probability export is standard in nnU-Net-family pipelines): V_mass = sum(p) (belief volume under calibration); V_commit = |{p > 0.5}| (the committed volume); V_opt = volume of the expected-Dice-maximizing binary prediction under the independent-voxel reading of p (a superlevel set; computable exactly per case by a threshold scan over sorted p — O(V log V), standard plug-in-rule computation). Case uncertainty U twofold: (a) mean binary entropy of p over the perfusion-deficit region (model-side), and (b) an image-side proxy computable with existing in-house machinery — mismatch diffuseness, (Tmax>6s volume − CBF<30% volume) and the fraction of deficit voxels in the boundary band. All scriptable today, no annotator.
candidates.use_vs_association: A controlled twin ablation separates 'the objective causes the hedge' from every data-side association: two networks identical in architecture, data, folds, seeds and schedule, differing ONLY in loss (cross-entropy twin vs soft-Dice-compound twin). Hedging is claimed only if the uncertainty-dependent committed-volume deficit appears in the Dice twin and not the CE twin, and if V_commit tracks the zero-parameter V_opt prediction rather than V_mass. Generic miscalibration, label noise, or cohort quirks load on both twins equally and cancel.
candidates.design_template_justification: The manipulated variable is the training objective — a single-factor, experimenter-controlled, training-time intervention. This is not cross-model-disagreement (the two models are not independent artifacts to be mined for disagreement; they are a matched pair constructed to differ in one factor) and no listed input-side grammar applies. First use of this grammar in the portfolio.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Lesion ground truth and model inputs coexist per case on a common grid so that twins can be trained and their per-case soft outputs scored, and the public cohort is locally trainable at small scale.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Archive member manifest (git show origin/results/probe-023-349af5ad0b3e:probes/023/results_v2/archive_manifest.csv, re-read 2026-09-02): 'train/derivatives/sub-stroke0001/ses-02/sub-stroke0001_ses-02_space-ncct_lesion-msk.nii.gz' alongside 'train/raw_data/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_ncct.nii.gz' and the four space-ncct perfusion maps; cohort-wide counts 149 lesion-bearing cases with maps and NCCT (probe-023 processed 99-100 cases end-to-end on this grid, evidence/decisions.md 2026-08-30). Local trainability of this cohort at winner-recipe scale is established by arXiv 2505.18424; small-scale twins are strictly lighter.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: Low-resolution twins must learn enough signal for volume behavior to be meaningful (the winner's hidden-test Dice of 28.5 shows the task is weakly but genuinely learnable). Gate: each twin must beat both an all-background predictor and a copy-the-Tmax>6s-mask baseline on held-out cases, or the audit is declared vacuous and stops.
candidates.dies_like_prior: No kill-table match: all 12 IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE kills involved patient-, acquisition-, or population-side covariates that could not be separated; here the manipulated variable is the training objective, which the experimenter controls — the twin design is randomization-equivalent by construction. No DATA_ACCESS exposure (public data, self-trained models). Distinct from this cycle's c02 (label-geometry audit): c02 audits what the labels contain; this audits the decision rule the objective installs.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Bertels et al. proved theoretically and on three tasks that soft-Dice-optimized maps carry an uncertainty-dependent volume bias while cross-entropy delivers unbiased volumes (Medical Image Analysis 2021, PMID 33075643 / arXiv 2211.04161), building on their MICCAI 2019 result (Optimization with soft Dice can lead to a volumetric bias). Recent decision-theory work formalizes expected-metric-optimal plug-in rules and the estimation-to-decision gap (arXiv 2604.13262). None of it audits a stroke challenge model as a revealed-preference forecaster on ISLES'24.
novelty_neighbors: Bertels, Robben, Vandermeulen, Suetens — 'Theoretical analysis and experimental validation of volume bias of soft Dice optimized segmentation maps in the context of inherent uncertainty', Medical Image Analysis 2021, PMID 33075643, arXiv 2211.04161 (found by search 2026-09-02)
Bertels et al. — 'Optimization with soft Dice can lead to a volumetric bias', MICCAI BrainLes 2019 (found by search 2026-09-02, via ResearchGate record 341488358)

'Rethinking Uncertainty in Segmentation: From Estimation to Decision', arXiv 2604.13262 (2026) — the estimation-to-decision gap and expected-metric-optimal plug-in (RankDice-family) rules (found by search 2026-09-02)
candidates.novelty_delta: Prior work proves the volume bias exists and proposes calibration fixes; nobody has audited a challenge-grade stroke model's committed-vs-belief volume gap as a behavioral policy — testing the zero-parameter expected-Dice-optimal prediction case-by-case — on ISLES'24, the public benchmark whose extreme inherent uncertainty (winning Dice 28.5) is precisely the regime where the theory says the hedge is largest, and whose official AVD metric prices the consequence.
candidates.why_not_done: BLIND_SPOT: the segmentation community files volume bias under 'calibration nuisance to be fixed', and the forecast-verification community's hedging concept never crossed into medical imaging — so trained segmenters' threshold behavior is tuned, not audited against the model's own stated beliefs. The enabling theory has existed since 2019; the framing is what was missing.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Train the CE/soft-Dice twins (compact patch-based 3D U-Net at reduced resolution, ~3-4 h each on a Colab GPU) on ~100 cases with 49 held out. Per held-out case and twin, compute V_mass, V_commit, V_opt, and U. Decisive readout: the interaction — the signed relative committed-volume deficit (V_commit − V_mass)/V_mass regressed on U must have a negative slope in the Dice twin and a ~zero slope in the CE twin (patient-bootstrap CIs), with V_commit agreeing with V_opt in the Dice twin. Label-using secondary in the official metric: per-case AVD of V_commit vs AVD of V_mass — does the belief volume beat the committed volume as a volume biomarker?
candidates.compute_envelope: Both twin trainings (~3-4 h each), inference, and CPU statistics fit one long Colab GPU session (~8-10 h on A100; two standard sessions on T4 as fallback, one per twin). The cycle's shared winner-recipe fold (c01 substrate) upgrades attribution toward 'the winning family' but is not required for the decision.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Site/protocol/population/prevalence: irrelevant — the contrast is between twins on identical data, within case. Optimization asymmetry between losses: equalized epochs, schedule, and early-stopping on the same validation split; both twins reported in full. Ground-truth label noise inflating apparent uncertainty: U is computed from model output and image-side proxies, never from labels. Patch-sampling suppression of small lesions: shared identically by both twins; results additionally reported by lesion-size stratum.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) Generic under-confidence in diffuse cases regardless of objective — excluded by the CE twin control. (2) A fixed-threshold artifact rather than learned sharpening — distinguished by the V_opt comparison: the theory predicts the Dice-trained map itself internalizes the bet, so V_commit at 0.5 should already sit near V_opt. (3) The actual winner's compound loss may hedge less than purer soft-Dice — scoped: the claim covers the loss family as trained here, with the winner-recipe fold as a named extension.
candidates.anticipated_negative: Decisive within the design: no Dice-vs-CE interaction means this loss family does not induce detectable uncertainty-dependent volume hedging at ISLES'24 noise levels — a citable certificate that challenge volumes may be read as beliefs, directly relevant to AVD interpretation.
candidates.annotation_burden: None. All quantities are computed by script from released data and self-trained models.

clarity.why: One-sentence question with three named, formula-defined volumes and a signed prediction; loses a point because 'case uncertainty' needs two operationalizations (model-side and image-side).

identifiability.why: The twin ablation isolates the objective as cause — the cleanest identification in this cycle — and the zero-parameter V_opt prediction separates hedging from generic miscalibration; short of 5 because transfer from the low-res twins to the actual winner is by family, not by identity.

medical_relevance.why: Infarct volume from segmentation is used as a biomarker and endpoint; showing it is a scoring-rule bet that shrinks in uncertain patients changes how such volumes may be reported clinically — and AVD is an official challenge metric.

interest.why: 'The model hedges like a badly scored weather forecaster' is a surprising, checkable reading of a familiar tool, with a quantitative signature rather than a vibe.

prior_legwork.why: Dataset staged and integrity-proven in-house; theory and plug-in algorithms published; but no trained fold exists yet and the twin harness is new code.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE; self-contained twins at reduced resolution; first decision in days on one Colab GPU.

data_readiness.why: Public staged data; known corrupt member and duplicate mask row governed by standing exclusion policy.

evaluation_readiness.why: AVD is an official challenge metric and the volume quantities are standard; only the interaction regression needs pre-registration.

negative_result_value.why: The twin control makes a null decisive for this loss family at this noise level, and the null is itself a useful calibration certificate.

novelty_confidence.why: The theory neighbors are close and well-identified; no audit of this shape found on any stroke benchmark, but search was limited — capped pending the novelty audit.

regret.why: The theory community could run this on any dataset; ISLES'24's extreme-uncertainty regime and our staging make it naturally ours, but it is not uniquely time-critical.

unverified_claims: Murphy's hedging formulation (meteorological forecast verification) cited as construct from memory; construct source, not load-bearing evidence
That the winner's compound Dice+CE loss behaves like purer soft-Dice in volume terms (checked inside the experiment, not assumed)
Colab session-length sufficiency for both twins in one session (fallback: one session per twin, still within envelope per twin)
candidates.plain_pitch: Weather forecasters who are graded with a badly designed score learn to report strategic forecasts instead of their honest beliefs — a phenomenon meteorology named 'hedging' decades ago. Stroke segmentation models are graded with exactly such a score (Dice), and theory says this quietly teaches them to commit to smaller lesions than their own internal evidence expects, most severely in the most uncertain patients. We train two otherwise-identical models — one graded the suspect way, one graded honestly — and check whether the suspect one's reported lesion volumes shrink below its own expectations exactly as the betting theory predicts. If true, the lesion volumes that stroke AI reports are bets, not beliefs, and should be corrected before anyone treats them as measurements.

candidates.title: Caught mid-swallow: does the model read acquisition luck as collateral biology?
candidates.question: Is the model using the CTA's snapshot timing — where in the patient's own contrast transit the angiogram happened to be caught — as if it were collateral biology, inheriting the single-phase timing fallacy that multiphase CTA was invented to escape?

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: The snapshot-timing / rolling-shutter artifact from photography and computational imaging: a single frame of a dynamic scene encodes when it was captured as much as what it depicts, and downstream consumers of the frame inherit that timing as if it were content.
cross_domain.implied_measurement: Treat the CTA as one frame of the movie the 4D CTP actually recorded: measure the snap phase (where the CTA sits on the patient's own arterial time-enhancement curve) and sweep it — re-rendering the angiographic channel from real acquired CTP frames at earlier and later phases — to read the model's dose-response to pure timing.
cross_domain.if_analogy_dropped: The candidate degrades to 'is the model robust to CTA acquisition variability' — still testable with the same machinery, but the specific prediction (early snap phase mimics poor collaterals, so predictions should inflate as phase moves earlier) loses its organizing physics.

candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using the CTA's acquisition timing — a protocol accident the full 4D perfusion input already determines — as if it were collateral biology, so early-triggered angiograms read as poor collaterals and inflate the predicted infarct.
candidates.X_measurement: Relative snap phase φ per case: correlate CTA enhancement over the released Circle-of-Willis arterial-mask voxels with each frame of the registered 4D CTP at the same voxels (all three volumes are released co-registered in NCCT space); φ = time offset of the best-matching frame from the patient's arterial peak. The sweep instrument: pseudo-CTAs composited from real acquired CTP frames at chosen offsets around φ, rendering held constant across the sweep. Both scriptable today, no annotator.
candidates.multi_step_causal_story: Link 1 (checkable, gate 0): the snap phase is measurable — CTA enhancement patterns pin to a specific segment of the patient's CTP time-enhancement curve. Link 2 (the experiment): a CTA-consuming model's prediction shifts with φ at fixed biology, because collateral conspicuity in a single-phase angiogram depends jointly on biology and timing. Link 3 (implied failure mode, exploratory): sites and protocols differ systematically in trigger timing, so φ-sensitivity becomes a site-level bias in deployed predictions.
candidates.use_vs_association: Within-patient dose-response: the same patient, the same fixed CTP and NCCT inputs, only the angiographic channel's capture phase varies — using genuinely acquired frames of that patient, not synthesis. Any monotone or peaked response of predicted volume to φ is use of timing by construction; cross-patient correlation of φ with severity never enters the primary readout. Crucially, the model retains the full 4D CTP input at every sweep point, so φ carries zero additional information about the patient — any residual φ-sensitivity is double-counting acquisition luck, not legitimate inference.
candidates.design_template_justification: An input intervention that substitutes genuinely acquired same-session frames — not counterfactual-synthesis (nothing is synthesized; every voxel shown to the model was measured in this patient at some real instant) and not idea-022's other:temporal-reparameterization (that grammar warps the CTP time axis the model consumes; here the CTP input is untouched and only the snapshot channel's capture time varies).
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Registered CTA, registered full 4D CTP, and arterial (CoW) masks coexist per case on the common NCCT grid, so the snap phase is computable and real-frame substitution is geometrically trivial.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Archive member manifest (git show origin/results/probe-023-349af5ad0b3e:probes/023/results_v2/archive_manifest.csv, read 2026-09-02): 'train/derivatives/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_space-ncct_cta.nii.gz' (15,120,317 bytes) and 'train/derivatives/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_space-ncct_ctp.nii.gz' (451,587,495 bytes — a full 4D series) and 'train/derivatives/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_space-ncct_cow-msk.nii.gz'; cohort-wide counts 149/149/149. Separate raw-space CTA and CTP members per case confirm the CTA is an independent acquisition, not a CTP derivative.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: (1) CTP temporal spacing (typically 1-2 s per frame, unverified here) bounds φ precision — gate 0 measures it on staged cases before anything else. (2) No public CTA-consuming ISLES'24 checkpoint exists; the model under test is a locally trained full-modality fold of the challenge's standard family (shared substrate with the cycle's c04 plan), and attribution is scoped accordingly. (3) The pseudo-CTA/real-CTA domain gap is real; the primary contrast is therefore strictly within the constant-rendering pseudo-CTA sweep, with the real CTA as an anchor point only.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Nearest kill: idea-037 (the scan remembers which hospital took it, IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE) — that design compared acquisition signatures across patients where site covaries with population; here the primary evidence is a within-patient dose-response with acquisition physics and anatomy held fixed. Nearest paused relative: idea-022 (end of scan vs end of bolus) — blocked on obtaining an external raw-4D checkpoint plus its training-time padding semantics; this candidate trains its own model, intervenes on a different channel (the angiographic snapshot, not CTP truncation), and includes a channel-ablation pre-gate proving the model actually consumes CTA. Idea-025 (actigraph, PAUSED) shares only the 'model reads acquisition state' family; its blocker (unobtainable pre-correction images) has no analogue here because every sweep frame is released data.
candidates.closest_prior_work: The clinical literature has established that single-phase CTA collateral assessment is timing-sensitive: automated collateral scores measurably depend on acquisition timing (Neuroradiology 2022, DOI 10.1007/s00234-022-03050-4); multiphase CTA exists precisely because single-phase snapshots understate delayed collateral filling (Menon et al., Radiology 2015, DOI 10.1148/radiol.15142256); and current work steers CTA timing using CTP time-enhancement curves (PMC12967852). None of it asks whether a trained final-infarct model inherits the fallacy.
novelty_neighbors: 'Time dependency of automated collateral scores in computed tomography angiography and computed tomography perfusion images in patients with intracranial arterial occlusion', Neuroradiology 2022, DOI 10.1007/s00234-022-03050-4 (found by search 2026-09-02)

Menon et al. — 'Multiphase CT angiography: a new tool for the imaging triage of patients with acute ischemic stroke', Radiology 2015, DOI 10.1148/radiol.15142256 (found by search 2026-09-02; construct anchor for single-phase timing sensitivity)

'Single-phase CTA guided by the time-enhancement curve derived from CT perfusion for mechanical thrombectomy', PMC12967852 (found by search 2026-09-02; the field is actively steering CTA timing off CTP curves)
candidates.novelty_delta: Prior work shows collateral scores depend on acquisition phase; no published work measures whether a trained final-infarct segmentation model inherits that dependence, and none performs a within-patient phase intervention using the patient's own acquired 4D frames at fixed biology.
candidates.why_not_done: NEW_CAPABILITY: the within-patient phase sweep needs co-registered single-phase CTA, a full 4D CTP series, and final-infarct ground truth released together per case — ISLES'24 is, to our knowledge, the first public stroke cohort shipping that combination (payload-verified 149/149/149 this stage), so the experiment only recently became possible outside a hospital PACS.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Gate 0 (CPU, one afternoon, label-blind): on 10 staged cases, measure CTP frame spacing, verify φ is identifiable (sharp CTA-to-frame matching over CoW voxels), and validate constant-rendering pseudo-CTA construction. Decisive run: for ~30 held-out-fold cases, sweep 5-7 phases each through the full-modality fold (~200 forward passes); readout: within-patient dose-response of predicted infarct volume (and of predicted extent on the collateral-dependent side) against φ, patient-cluster bootstrap; the real-CTA prediction must sit near the pseudo-CTA at the measured φ for the anchor check.
candidates.compute_envelope: Given the cycle's shared full-modality fold (planned once for c04/c07/c08, 1-2 GPU-days, outside this envelope but shared cycle infrastructure), gate 0 plus the full sweep and analysis fit one Colab GPU session. Standalone fallback within one long session: a reduced-resolution three-channel (NCCT+CTA+Tmax) U-Net trained ~4-5 h, then a 15-case × 5-phase sweep — decisive at reduced sensitivity.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Injection protocol, cardiac output, site, scanner: cancelled within patient — every sweep point is the same acquisition. Venous overlay at late phases mimicking collateral filling: composited frames restricted to the pre-venous window identified from the whole-brain time-enhancement curve, late phases reported separately. The model ignoring the CTA channel entirely: channel-ablation pre-gate; if CTA contributes nothing, the candidate dies cheaply at that gate and the null is reported. Labels: never enter the primary readout.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) The model reacts to pseudo-CTA rendering artifacts, not phase — controlled by constant rendering across the sweep and the real-CTA anchor point. (2) φ-sensitivity as legitimate inference — excluded by construction: the full CTP input is present and unchanged at every sweep point, so the snapshot's phase adds no information about the patient; reacting to it is double-counting. (3) Registration residuals between channels — identical registered volumes are used at every sweep point, so residuals are constant and cancel in the within-patient contrast.
candidates.anticipated_negative: A flat φ-response, bounded by the gate-0 phase precision, is a genuinely useful robustness certificate: it would say this model family extracts timing-invariant content from single-phase CTA — evidence the single-phase timing fallacy does not propagate into this class of stroke AI.

clarity.why: One-sentence question with a defined phase variable and a signed prediction; a point off because 'collateral conspicuity' as the mediating channel is named but not itself isolated at this rung.

identifiability.why: Within-patient dose-response on real acquired frames with rendering and all other channels fixed, plus the information-theoretic argument that φ is redundant given full CTP; residuals are the pseudo-CTA domain gap and locally-trained-model attribution, both scoped.

medical_relevance.why: Collateral reading drives thrombectomy triage, and trigger timing varies by site and protocol; a model that inherits the timing fallacy carries a deployable, correctable site bias — and the fix (phase-conditioning or multiphase input) is concrete.

interest.why: 'The AI grades your collaterals worse because the tech triggered early' is an eyebrow-raiser with a named clinical ancestor (the single-phase fallacy) and a clean intervention.

prior_legwork.why: Staging, registration, and CoW masks are released and verified; deficit machinery exists in-house; but the phase-matching and compositing instruments are new code and the full-modality fold does not exist yet.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE, but the decisive run depends on the shared full-modality fold or the reduced standalone fallback, and gate 0 could still reveal φ to be poorly identifiable at released temporal resolution.

data_readiness.why: All required members payload-verified per case (149/149/149) on a proven staging pipeline; the 4D volumes are large (~450 MB/case) but a 30-case subset is ~14 GB, well within a session.

evaluation_readiness.why: Custom dose-response readout requiring pre-registered phase offsets and margins; no external benchmark applies to the sweep itself.

negative_result_value.why: Sensitivity-limited by phase precision, but gate 0 converts that into a stated floor before any model work, so the null is bounded, not empty.

novelty_confidence.why: Close clinical neighbors exist and are cited; no model-behavior version found in limited search — capped pending the novelty audit.

regret.why: The enabling data combination is public; another group could run this, but the clinical-AI community has not framed it, so the window is comfortable rather than urgent.

unverified_claims: CTP temporal frame spacing and total coverage in the released series (gate-0 measurement; manifest proves existence and size, not sampling)
That the released space-ncct CTA is contrast-phase-diverse across the cohort (expected from multi-center acquisition; checked as a by-product of gate 0)
That maximum-intensity compositing of CTP frames yields angiographically usable pseudo-CTAs at CTP spatial resolution (gate-0 validation)
candidates.plain_pitch: A CT angiogram is a single photograph of dye flowing through the brain's arteries, and like any photo of a moving scene, it depends on the instant the shutter fired: caught early, healthy detour vessels haven't filled yet and look absent — a known trap that leads human readers to underrate a patient's backup blood supply. This dataset also contains the full movie of the same dye transit, so we can tell exactly when each patient's photo was snapped, and even re-create the photo at earlier or later instants from real recorded frames. We ask whether a stroke-outcome model shown the same patient with only the snapshot instant changed predicts different amounts of dead brain — which would mean it mistakes camera timing for biology. If it does, hospitals with different injection protocols would get systematically different AI predictions for identical patients; if it doesn't, that is a real robustness credential this field currently cannot claim.

candidates.title: The model speaks one vendor's dialect: swap the deconvolution, keep the patient
candidates.question: Is the model using icobrain's dialect of the perfusion maps — the algorithm-specific rendering of delay sensitivity and regularization — rather than the hemodynamics beneath, so its predictions move when the same raw bolus movie is deconvolved by a different published formula?

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: The inter-laboratory round-robin from metrology: the same specimen measured by different certified instruments decomposes observed variance into specimen-borne and instrument-borne components (gauge R&R). Here the specimen is the patient's raw 4D bolus movie, the instruments are deconvolution algorithms, and the 'measurement' being audited is the trained model's prediction.
cross_domain.implied_measurement: Hold the patient fixed and swap the instrument: recompute the perfusion maps from the released raw 4D series with two published deconvolution formulas from the two algorithm classes known to drive inter-software disagreement (delay-sensitive standard SVD, Østergaard 1996; delay-insensitive block-circulant SVD, Wu et al. 2003), and measure the paired shift in the model's predicted infarct.
cross_domain.if_analogy_dropped: Without the round-robin frame this is still a robustness test, but it loses the variance-decomposition target — how much of the model's output is patient versus instrument — which is the number a deployer actually needs.

candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using the map-maker's dialect: a measurable share of its predicted infarct moves when the same patient's raw bolus movie is rendered by a different published deconvolution — so challenge-trained stroke models do not transfer across perfusion software without recalibration.
candidates.X_measurement: Paired map dialects from identical raw data: (a) the released icobrain space-ncct maps; (b) maps recomputed from the released registered 4D CTP by delay-sensitive sSVD and (c) by delay-insensitive block-circulant SVD — both textbook formulas implementable in numpy/scipy — with the arterial input function selected automatically from released Circle-of-Willis mask voxels. The two SVD variants also give a within-family dose axis (regularization threshold) for a same-dialect perturbation floor. All scriptable today, no annotator.
candidates.use_vs_association: Within-patient paired intervention on the processing chain with anatomy, acquisition, and physiology bit-identical across arms — the exact identification pattern ratified in the idea-004 arc. A paired prediction delta under dialect swap is, by construction, use of dialect-specific map content, not correlation with any patient property; the primary contrast (sSVD vs bcSVD) is between two published formulas, so our own implementation quality is not the manipulated variable.
candidates.design_template_justification: First use of this grammar in the isles24 charter: same acquisition, two processing chains, paired model-output comparison — a deliberate transplant of the completed and ratified idea-004 paradigm (CT-RATE reconstruction-pair study, finding of record: the model uses reconstruction-dependent content) from chest-CT classification to stroke segmentation, where the processing chain is the deconvolution algorithm instead of the scanner kernel.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: The raw 4D CTP series, the vendor-derived maps, the arterial masks, and the lesion ground truth coexist per case (registered), so dialect maps can be computed from identical raw data and fed to the same model on the same grid.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Archive member manifest (git show origin/results/probe-023-349af5ad0b3e:probes/023/results_v2/archive_manifest.csv, read 2026-09-02): per case both 'train/raw_data/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_ctp.nii.gz' (native 4D) and 'train/derivatives/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_space-ncct_ctp.nii.gz' (registered 4D, 451,587,495 bytes) plus the four icobrain space-ncct maps and 'sub-stroke0001_ses-01_space-ncct_cow-msk.nii.gz'; cohort counts 149 registered 4D CTP, 149 raw 4D CTP, 149 CoW masks. The icobrain chain and its undocumented-units finding are established in-house (evidence/decisions.md 2026-08-26).
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: (1) The released 4D series' preprocessing state (baseline pre-contrast frames present, motion handling) is uninspected — gate 0 reads headers and time-enhancement curves on staged cases before any deconvolution. (2) Our sSVD/bcSVD maps will differ from icobrain in absolute scale — absorbed by the model family's per-channel z-scoring at preprocessing time, and the primary contrast is between our two dialects, with icobrain-vs-ours as a caveated secondary arm. (3) A full-modality (map-consuming) fold must exist — shared cycle substrate, same as c04/c07.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Nearest kill: idea-037 (hospital signature, IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE) died because site covaries with population across patients; here the processing swap is within-patient with everything else bit-identical — the defense that carried idea-004 to a ratified finding. Idea-029 (the ground truth remembers the algorithm, killed): concerned algorithm provenance of the LABELS; labels are untouched here and never enter the primary readout. Sibling disclosure: backlog isles24-scout-001-c08 ('the deconvolution algorithm may have signed the image', SCOUT_ONLY, never developed) asks whether the algorithm's signature exists in the image; this candidate asks whether a trained model's behavior depends on it, via a paired intervention along a named algorithm-class axis — if that backlog card is ever developed it is the image-side companion, not a duplicate.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Kudo et al. showed that commercial CTP software packages produce significantly different maps from identical source data, with delay-sensitivity the organizing factor (Radiology 2010, PMID 20032153); AJNR 2012;33:2074 replicated summary-map divergence between two packages; and Scientific Reports 2023 (DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-48700-6) showed lesion thresholds must be recalibrated between deconvolution algorithms. All quantify map-level variability; none measures a trained deep segmentation model's paired behavioral response to the swap.
novelty_neighbors: Kudo et al. — 'Differences in CT perfusion maps generated by different commercial software: quantitative analysis by using identical source data of acute stroke patients', Radiology 2010, PMID 20032153, DOI 10.1148/radiol.254082000 (found by search 2026-09-02)
'CT perfusion stroke lesion threshold calibration between deconvolution algorithms', Scientific Reports 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-48700-6 (found by search 2026-09-02)
'Differences in CT perfusion summary maps for patients with acute ischemic stroke generated by 2 software packages', AJNR 2012;33:2074 (found by search 2026-09-02)
candidates.novelty_delta: The map-level variability is settled science; the open question — whether a challenge-trained deep final-infarct model's predictions move under a within-patient deconvolution swap, and by how much relative to a same-dialect perturbation floor — has, per this limited search, never been measured on any public stroke benchmark.
candidates.why_not_done: NEW_CAPABILITY plus BLIND_SPOT: measuring it requires raw 4D source data, vendor maps, and ground truth released together at cohort scale, which ISLES'24 provides first (payload-verified); and inside any single benchmark the dialect variable is invisible precisely because every case ships one vendor's maps — the uniformity that enables clean training is the uniformity that hides the fragility.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Gate 0 (CPU): stage ~10 registered 4D volumes (~4.5 GB), inspect temporal axes and baseline frames, implement sSVD and bcSVD, and sanity-check dialect maps against released icobrain maps (within-brain rank correlation — plausibility, not agreement). Decisive run: 30 paired cases × three map dialects through the shared full-modality fold (~90 forward passes); readout: per-case cross-dialect prediction Dice and volume shift versus the within-dialect regularization-perturbation floor, patient-cluster bootstrap; secondary: where disagreement concentrates (deficit boundary vs interior).
candidates.compute_envelope: Deconvolution is CPU-cheap (minutes per case at map resolution); with the shared full-modality fold, staging + deconvolution + inference + analysis for 30 cases fit one Colab GPU session. Standalone fallback: the same reduced-resolution multi-channel U-Net fallback as c07 (~4-5 h), then a 15-case swap in the same session.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Scanner/site/protocol/population: cancelled — the swap is within patient on identical raw data. Absolute scale differences between dialects: absorbed by per-channel z-scoring in the standard preprocessing, so surviving deltas are structural, not offset; residual scale interaction reported. Our implementation quality: the primary axis is published-formula vs published-formula (sSVD vs bcSVD), with the same code path, same AIF, same grid — only the documented algorithmic difference (delay handling) varies; icobrain-vs-ours is secondary and caveated. Labels: untouched in the primary readout. The known source-corrupt member (sub-stroke0043 CBF) and duplicate lesion row: standing exclusion policy applies.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) Deltas reflect our deconvolution being noisy rather than dialect content — bounded by the within-dialect perturbation floor: the claim requires cross-dialect shift to exceed same-dialect regularization jitter. (2) The model barely reads the map channels at all (NCCT dominates) — a channel-ablation pre-gate quantifies map reliance first; a model that ignores maps yields a cheap, reportable null. (3) AIF selection differences masquerading as algorithm differences — AIF is computed once per patient from the released CoW mask and shared verbatim across dialect arms.
candidates.anticipated_negative: Valuable either way: prediction invariance across the dialect swap (relative to the perturbation floor) is a portability certificate no stroke-segmentation model currently holds — direct evidence the model reads vendor-invariant hemodynamic content; the idea-004 precedent shows the paired design is sensitive enough to detect real processing dependence when it exists.

clarity.why: One-sentence question with a named manipulated variable (deconvolution algorithm class) and a paired readout; a point off because 'dialect' bundles delay handling, regularization, and vendor postprocessing, only the first two of which we can manipulate.

identifiability.why: Within-patient bit-identical pairing plus a same-dialect perturbation floor isolates processing-borne content — the 004-ratified pattern; short of 5 because the icobrain arm (the actual vendor) can only be compared against our implementations, not swapped like-for-like.

medical_relevance.why: Hospitals run different perfusion software (RAPID, syngo, olea, icobrain); whether challenge-trained models transfer across them is a direct deployment-safety question, and the answer comes with an effect size.

interest.why: After the 004 arc, 'models read processing-dependent content' is expected in-house; the surprise here is the magnitude on a task where the maps are the canonical clinical input — solid, but the least eyebrow-raising of the three.

prior_legwork.why: The complete 004 interpretive machinery (paired deltas, patient-cluster bootstrap, perturbation-floor logic) transfers; staging proven; CoW masks solve AIF selection; formulas published.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE, but honest deconvolution engineering (baseline handling, motion, partial volume in the AIF) plus the shared-fold dependency put the first decision at ~2-3 weeks, not days.

data_readiness.why: All members payload-verified (149 raw + 149 registered 4D, masks, maps); volumes are large but subset staging is proven.

evaluation_readiness.why: Paired prediction-Dice and volume-shift readouts are standard, but the perturbation-floor margin must be pre-registered; no external benchmark applies.

negative_result_value.why: A floor-bounded invariance result is a publishable portability certificate — the null is close to decisive for this model family and dialect axis.

novelty_confidence.why: Map-level neighbors are settled and close; no model-behavior version found in limited search — capped pending the novelty audit.

regret.why: Any group with the dataset could do this, but only after implementing deconvolution and training a fold; our staged assets make it cheap for us specifically.

unverified_claims: Preprocessing state of the released 4D series — baseline frames, motion handling (gate-0 header and curve inspection)
That per-channel z-scoring is what the shared full-modality fold's preprocessing actually does to map inputs (checked against the pipeline configuration before the decisive run)
Østergaard 1996 / Wu et al. 2003 bibliographic details cited from standard usage; the formulas themselves are textbook and independently checkable
candidates.plain_pitch: The colored 'blood-flow maps' doctors use in stroke are not raw measurements: software computes them from a movie of dye passing through the brain, and it is well documented that different vendors' software turns the identical movie into visibly different maps. This dataset uniquely ships both the raw movie and one vendor's maps, so we can recompute the maps with different published recipes and show the very same patient to a stroke-prediction model in several software 'dialects'. If the model's predicted dead-tissue region shifts with the dialect, then models trained on this benchmark are partly reading the software's accent rather than the patient's blood flow — and moving such a model to a hospital that runs different software would silently change its predictions. If the predictions hold still, that is a portability credential no stroke AI currently has.

dropped.question: [economics: hedonic pricing] Is the benchmark using a flat value function — errors priced identically in the internal capsule and in silent white matter — while the released 3-month mRS prices them apart?
dropped.why: The novelty search surfaced a directly adverse result in this exact population: in the HERMES anterior-LVO cohort, accounting for lesion location did NOT strengthen the follow-up-volume-to-mRS association (Neuroradiology 2021, DOI 10.1007/s00234-021-02784-x), against mixed positive evidence elsewhere (Cheng et al., Stroke 2014, PMID 24781084); with n=149 and heavy mRS confounding (age, NIHSS, reperfusion), the surviving model-error-geography arm alone is too thin to carry a card this cycle.

dropped.question: [ecology/climate science: early-warning signals] Does penumbral tissue near collapse show critical slowing down — rising temporal autocorrelation in its 4D enhancement residuals — and does the model read it?
dropped.why: One step past defensible, and it fails the measurement test: physiological state fluctuations would have to be read under a contrast-dominated signal sampled at roughly 0.5 Hz, and inferring dynamics from effectively snapshot data is the exact pattern that killed idea-020 (IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE).

dropped.question: [cardiology/signal processing: heart-rate-variability analysis] Is the model reading atrial fibrillation — the stroke's embolic cause — as beat-to-beat jitter written into the 4D contrast enhancement?
dropped.why: One step past defensible: CTP frame spacing is on the order of the cardiac RR interval, so beat-to-beat irregularity is aliased below measurability; the cardiac-systemic channel is already represented in the backlog by isles24-scout-004-c03 (the heart's signature in the head scan).

dropped.question: [electrical network theory: effective resistance] Does the Circle-of-Willis graph's effective resistance between inflow and the occluded territory predict what the model spares?
dropped.why: Cross-patient anatomy classification is the exact grammar of killed ideas 032 and 036 (IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE, both): CoW anatomy covaries with population and protocol across patients, and no within-patient contrast exists because a patient has one fixed anatomy; nothing about the released CoW masks changes that identification problem.

dropped.question: [forensic accounting: Benford/digit forensics] Do the perfusion maps' value distributions carry a processing watermark — and is the model reading the watermark rather than the physiology?
dropped.why: With a single uniform icobrain chain across the cohort there is no watermark variance to exploit observationally (the cross-patient version is the killed idea-037 family); the actionable interventional version of this question is exactly candidate c08's paired dialect swap, which supersedes it.
